s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent pustular eruptions on the face with exacerbation by sunlight exposure
salient_findings: Recurrent pustular eruptions on the face
Failed response to broad-spectrum sunscreens, topical/oral antibiotics, and topical ivermectin
Intrafollicular and subcorneal pustule formation on histopathology
key_facts: 4-year history of recurrent pustular eruptions on the face
Eruptions initially occurred during a Florida vacation
Mild associated pruritus without burning sensation
Intermittent occurrence with erythematous papules and prominent pustules
Exacerbation by sunlight exposure, especially in summer months
Resolution within 3-4 days, leaving mild background erythema by 5-7 days
Failed response to broad-spectrum sunscreens, topical/oral antibiotics, and topical ivermectin
No joint pain, fever, fatigue, changes in urine color, medication use, or rashes elsewhere
No significant medical history
Numerous 1-2mm monomorphous pustules over background erythema on medial cheeks, chin, and nose
Negative serum antinuclear antibodies
Negative anti-SSA/Ro antibodies
Negative anti-SSB/La antibodies
Negative bacterial swab from malar lesions
Negative periodic acid–Schiff stain for fungal organisms
Negative Grocott methenamine silver stain for fungal organisms
Intrafollicular and subcorneal pustule formation on histopathology

shortlist.label: Polymorphic light eruption
shortlist.why_kept: Exacerbation by sunlight exposure, especially in summer months

shortlist.label: Pustular psoriasis
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent pustular eruptions on the face with intrafollicular and subcorneal pustule formation on histopathology

shortlist.label: Subcorneal pustular dermatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Intrafollicular and subcorneal pustule formation on histopathology

shortlist.label: Eosinophilic pustular folliculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent pustular eruptions on the face with follicular involvement

shortlist.label: Pityrosporum folliculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent pustular eruptions on the face with follicular involvement and negative bacterial and fungal swabs

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of recurrent pustular eruptions on the face, exacerbation by sunlight exposure, and resolution within a few days are consistent with polymorphic light eruption. The lack of response to broad-spectrum sunscreens also supports this diagnosis, as polymorphic light eruption can be resistant to sunscreen protection.

rejected.label: Pustular psoriasis
rejected.why: Pustular psoriasis typically presents with more widespread and severe lesions, and is often accompanied by systemic symptoms such as fever and fatigue, which are not present in this case.

rejected.label: Subcorneal pustular dermatosis
rejected.why: Subcorneal pustular dermatosis is a rare condition that typically presents with sterile pustules, but it is not typically exacerbated by sunlight exposure.

rejected.label: Eosinophilic pustular folliculitis
rejected.why: Eosinophilic pustular folliculitis is a condition that typically presents with follicular pustules, but it is often accompanied by other symptoms such as fever and lymphadenopathy, which are not present in this case.

rejected.label: Pityrosporum folliculitis
rejected.why: Pityrosporum folliculitis is a condition caused by a fungal infection, but the negative periodic acid-Schiff stain and Grocott methenamine silver stain for fungal organisms make this diagnosis unlikely.
